What makes the sea turtle so amazing?

Swimming across the wide ocean, the sea turtle is a mysterious animal that journeys a long way back to the beach where it was born to lay its eggs.

content.alt: Sea turtle - Nature and science facts about the sea turtle
content.text:
Nature and science facts about the sea turtle

The sea turtle's legs are shaped like flippers (paddles), so it can swim far across the wide ocean (unlike a land tortoise, it can't pull its head into its shell). The most mysterious thing is that when a female lays her eggs, she returns to the very beach where she was born. At night she digs a hole in the sand and lays her eggs, and the baby turtles push their way out of the sand on their own and scurry off to the sea. They live a long time, but they need protection because of ocean trash.

Point out things like the flipper legs (swimming), returning to the beach, nesting at night, and ocean protection. Talking together about "How does it find its way back to where it was born?" is a great idea.

Parent guide — how to spark curiosity

Compare the wonder of "returning to where it was born to lay eggs" with the way salmon return home. Talking about "let's reduce ocean trash" helps grow a caring heart for the environment.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. How does a sea turtle find its way back to where it was born?
A. When a female lays her eggs, she journeys a long way back to the very beach where she was born.

Q. Why does a sea turtle need protection?
A. It's an animal that lives a very long time, but it is in danger because of ocean trash.

Q. How can we observe it at home?
A. It's great to compare it with the way salmon return home, and to talk about "reducing ocean trash."
